says: Welcome to Dunmere, traveller. Few come to us who aren't asking for something.
We keep to ourselves here. The realm's quarrels are the realm's; my walls are mine.
But I am not blind. Something stirs in the north, past Castle Grimhold, and the roads grow dangerous.
If you mean to set it right, Dunmere's gate is open to you, and my healer's hands are yours.

folk.says: The Duke is not to be crowded. That means you.
Stand where I can see you, and we'll get along.
Petitioners wait their turn. You're the turn, it seems.
Doors behind the throne: the feast hall, and the library. Stair to the cells is yonder.
The Duke's day is full. Though for one who rides against the north, it can be made less full.
The Duke listens to everyone and agrees with no one. It's quite maddening.
Grimhold sent an envoy last spring. He left without his horse. Nobody says why.
Linens to the chambers, ale to the barracks, and never a moment to sit.
I carry the Duke's letters! Well. I carry them to the man who carries them.
A song of Dunmere? It stood when the north fell, and it'll stand again. That's the whole song.
Came to sell the Duke iron. He bought it, too. Paid in coin, not promises, unlike Riverhold.
